items.name: the thyrsus
items.description: The ivy-wreathed Bacchic wand carried by worshippers; Pentheus takes Dionysus's wand and later carries one in disguise.

wikipedia.lead: In Ancient Greece a thyrsus or thyrsos was a wand or staff of giant fennel (Ferula communis) covered with ivy vines and leaves, sometimes wound with taeniae and topped with a pine cone, artichoke, fennel, or by a bunch of vine-leaves and grapes or ivy-leaves and berries, carried during Hellenic festivals and religious ceremonies. The thyrsus is typically associated with the Greek god Dionysus (and his subsequent Roman equivalent Bacchus) as a symbol of prosperity, fertility, and hedonism.

items.name: the timbrel
items.description: The hand drum of the Bacchic rites, said to be invented by Rhea and the Corybantes, played by the chorus.

items.name: the fawnskin
items.description: Spotted fawn-skin worn by Bacchic worshippers, which the old men and disguised Pentheus put on.

wikipedia.lead: Nebris is a small genus of marine ray-finned fishes belonging to the family Sciaenidae, the drums and croakers. There are two species in the genus, one in the Western Atlantic Ocean and one in the Eastern Pacific Ocean.
